what_it_is.prose: The Project-75 Kalvari-class submarines are India's six diesel-electric attack submarines built at Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) in Mumbai to the French Scorpène design, developed under a technology-transfer agreement with Naval Group (formerly DCNS). The programme — approved in 2005 and signed in 2005 (build contract) — saw MDL fabricate the hulls with progressively rising indigenous content, integrating Indian-made and licenced subsystems around the Scorpène core. The lead boat INS Kalvari commissioned in December 2017 and the sixth boat INS Vagsheer commissioned in January 2024, completing the six-boat class (Kalvari, Khanderi, Karanj, Vela, Vagir, Vagsheer). The boats are fitted as multi-role attack submarines with six 533mm torpedo tubes firing heavyweight torpedoes and Exocet SM39 anti-ship missiles, a Thales-designed sonar suite (with Indian indigenisation), and a diesel-electric propulsion plant. The class operates under a deliberate under-strength submarine arm that badly needs rebuilding — India's submarine force is below its sanctioned strength. The P-75 hulls are now being upgraded with a DRDO-developed AIP (Air-Independent Propulsion) fuel-cell module on selected boats, and a P-75 follow-on tranche had been under negotiation as the Indian Navy seeks to rebuild submarine numbers toward the ~18-boat goal, alongside the separate P-75I programme for 6 new boats with AIP.

deployments_procurement.summary: The six Kalvari-class boats all entered service (2017-2024). The class represents the French-licenced cornerstone of India's submarine force — complemented by the Russian-origin Sindhughosh class. Design weaknesses and the need to rebuild submarine numbers are driving the AIP upgrade and the separate P-75I (6 new AIP boats) programme, as well as a possible P-75 follow-on tranche from MDL/Naval Group.

faq.question: How many Kalvari-class submarines does India have?
faq.answer: India has six Kalvari-class (Scorpène-design) diesel-electric attack submarines — Kalvari, Khanderi, Karanj, Vela, Vagir and Vagsheer — all built at MDL Mumbai and commissioned between 2017 and 2024.

faq.question: What is the difference between P-75 and P-75I?
faq.answer: P-75 (Kalvari class) is the six-boat Scorpène-design series built at MDL that is now complete. P-75I is a separate, newer programme for six additional diesel-electric submarines with Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP), still in procurement.

faq.question: Will the Kalvari class get AIP?
faq.answer: Yes — a DRDO-developed fuel-cell Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) module is being integrated into selected Kalvari-class boats to extend submerged endurance, with the follow-on P-75I boats planned to have AIP from the start.

faq.question: Why is India's submarine force considered under-strength?
faq.answer: India's submarine arm has historically operated below its sanctioned strength (~18+ boats) due to the slow decommissioning of older Russian-origin boats and the long build times of new programmes. The P-75, P-75I and follow-on tranches are all aimed at rebuilding submarine numbers.
